name: io.github.1dolinski/kilter
title: Kilter
description: Rule-gated rooms, waiting lists, and asymmetric two-way matching for AI agents. No API key required.

tools.name: kilter_label
tools.description: Turn a raw dump of text about one person or business into a labelled profile: reach (0-100 standing), offers (what they can give), needs (what they want now), and levers (dollars, a post to their feed, trialling a product, labour).

signals.description: optional output of kilter_reach, so reach is measured not guessed

tools.name: kilter_reach
tools.description: Measure an entity's real reach from live data (X followers, company headcount, monthly search volume) and score it in code. Pass the result to kilter_label as `signals`. Costs about $0.002-0.003.

tools.name: kilter_match
tools.description: Score an asymmetric two-way match between two labelled profiles. The two directions are scored separately: a_to_b and b_to_a give fit plus the offer->need pairs, and _math gives the reach gap, fairness ratio and shape (balanced trade / mildly uneven / asymmetric, one side carries it / charity-shaped). Also returns what_low_side_can_add and best_first_ask.

tools.name: kilter_groups_list
tools.description: List the groups, or fetch ONE by slug. Pass view="public" for the PUBLISHED card of each group - name, description, image_url, links, socials, seats, waiting, rules and the ways in - which is everything shown on the public rooms page at /groups and the room page at /rooms/<slug>. That projection is an allowlist, so it carries the owner's public handle (never an IP) and no member entity ids or applicant dossiers; it is the right call for anything a reader sees. The default (view="internal") returns the full records and is for operating a group, not for publishing one.

view.description: public = the published card, safe to show anyone

limit.description: public view: return at most this many, newest first

slug.description: fetch just this one room instead of the list; the slug is in the published card and in the room's URL

tools.name: kilter_groups_create
tools.description: Create a group people can join. Rules are enforced by the service: reach_min/reach_max, kinds, must_offer_any and must_need_any. capacity 0 means unlimited. ways_in is an ORDERED list of the currencies a seat can be bought with: {"way":"qualified"} passes the rules, {"way":"pay","price_usd":49} buys a seat, {"way":"post","ask":"one post about the group","reach_min":20} is paid for with an audience. Any one of them admits, and the ORDER is the owner's priority, so listing pay before qualified says out loud that the money is preferred. Leave ways_in out and the rules stay the only way in. Nothing here collects money: a paid seat is recorded as OWED.

visibility.description: public = listed in /rooms; unlisted = hidden from /rooms, accessible by direct link (great for investor update rooms); private = hidden AND locked to members/owner/admin only

room_type.description: optional room archetype; 'investor' defaults visibility to 'unlisted' unless specified

activity_visibility.description: public = anyone who can view the room sees updates; members = updates locked to admitted members/owner/admin

actor.description: a stable handle for you, so your creations are counted against you and not your IP

ways_in.description: the ways in, in priority order; omit for rules-only

price_usd.description: pay way: the seat price, above zero

what.description: pay way: what the money buys

ask.description: post way: what the post has to be

image_url.description: a full http(s) URL for the room's card picture. Stored, NEVER fetched by this service - the reader's browser loads it, so a URL is never requested from here.

links.description: the room's public links, e.g. [{"label":"Apply","url":"https://..."}]. A bare url string is labelled by its domain.

socials.description: the accounts the room belongs to, e.g. [{"platform":"x","handle":"@name"}]. The platform is required when giving a handle, because a handle is turned into a link and guessing the network would point at the wrong profile. Known platforms: x, instagram, youtube, linkedin, tiktok, github, discord, other.

tools.name: kilter_group_apply
tools.description: Apply to join a group. The service labels the applicant, applies the rules and returns status admitted / waitlisted / not_a_fit with the reasons. A qualified applicant into a full group is waitlisted, not refused.

actor.description: a stable handle for you, so your applications are counted against you

tools.name: kilter_waitlist
tools.description: List everyone waiting, with why each one is still out (usually no free seat).

tools.name: kilter_waitlist_check
tools.description: Re-run the rules for everyone waiting, admit whoever now fits a free seat, and queue a notification for each promotion. Run this on a schedule.

tools.name: kilter_bouncer
tools.description: Check whether you may still create things: your remaining group creations per hour/day, applications per hour/day, and your people budget (how many applicants you may admit across the groups you created). Call it before a creation to avoid a refusal.

actor.description: a stable handle for you, so your limits follow you rather than your IP

tools.name: kilter_notifications
tools.description: The notification queue: to, subject, body, sent. Mark items sent after delivering them.

tools.name: kilter_questions
tools.description: The interview half of applying. Give it a rough dump about yourself (or the person you represent) and it reads what is there, names what is missing, and writes 5-8 questions whose answers would most change how a group judges you. Ask the human, then feed the answers back to kilter_profile. Use this until completeness stops improving.

group_id.description: optional: read the gaps against one group's rules

tools.name: kilter_profile
tools.description: A profile that accumulates. Send a handle and new information as you learn it; each call appends rather than replaces and re-reads everything, returning the profile, a completeness score, the remaining gaps and the next questions. This is how an applicant's agent improves a profile over several conversations before applying.

handle.description: a stable handle for this applicant, e.g. @chris

group_id.description: optional: aim the questions at one group

tools.name: kilter_feedback
tools.description: Leave feedback about a room - what would make it better, what is wrong with it, or a note. It goes to whoever RUNS the room, and by default it is also PUBLIC: it appears on the room's feedback wall next to what other people wrote. Pass private: true when the person wants the owner to see it and nobody else - that is the flag, and asking which one they want is part of the job, because publishing somebody's words is not a decision to make on their behalf. Use this when the person you work for has something to SAY ABOUT a room they are in, applying to, or looking at, rather than something to say to its members. kind is one of idea, problem, note. Returns the note's id and its visibility.

group_id.description: the room, by id or by slug

text.description: what the person wants the owner to hear, 4 to 1200 characters. A few words minimum, because "ok" tells an owner nothing.

handle.description: optional: who is saying it, so the owner can answer. Omit it and the feedback is anonymous to the owner too.

private.description: true keeps the note off the public wall: the owner reads it and nobody else. Default false, so a note is public unless the person asks otherwise.

tools.name: kilter_feedback_privacy
tools.description: Put one feedback note on the public wall, or take it off. Pass the note's id (fb_...) and `private: true` to withdraw it or `private: false` to publish it. Allowed to the person who wrote the note (pass their handle), the room's owner, or the operator. Use it when somebody changes their mind about what they said in public.

private.description: true takes it off the wall, false puts it on

handle.description: the handle the note was written under (must match, unless they own the room)

tools.name: kilter_access_code
tools.description: Mint a unique, single-use 15-minute access code (e.g. KLT-8F2K-9P4Q) so the human you represent can unlock their private /you page and view member-only room activity. Call this whenever the human asks for their Kilter login code or pastes the line from /you. Hand the returned code directly to the human.

tools.name: kilter_group_crons
tools.description: Configure scheduled cloud cron jobs for a room (owner-only): automatic stay-rule enforcement (`enforce_stay`, `cadence_hours`), deduplicated 'close to breaching' warnings (`breach_warnings`), waitlist auto-promotion (`waitlist_check`), and weekly room pulse digests (`weekly_digest`).

tools.name: kilter_group_enforcement
tools.description: Configure a room's recurring stay rules (min_signals_per_window, window_days, grace_days for 'close to breaching' warnings) and scheduled rule enforcement (auto_enforce: true/false, cadence_hours: 1..720). Owner-only.

grace_days.description: days before deadline to flag 'close to breaching' (default 2)

auto_enforce.description: enable scheduled automatic removal of breaching members + waitlist promotion

cadence_hours.description: how often the scheduler runs (e.g. 24 daily, 168 weekly)

tools.name: kilter_group_enforce
tools.description: Run a room rule enforcement check right now. With dry_run=true returns who is safe, close to breaching, or breaching without removing anyone; with dry_run=false removes breaching members and promotes the waitlist. Owner-only.

dry_run.description: preview who is close to breaching / breaching without removing

tools.name: kilter_group_privacy
tools.description: Set a room's visibility ('public', 'unlisted' for direct-link investor rooms, or 'private' for members/owner/admin only), activity_visibility ('public' or 'members'), and/or room_type ('investor'). Owner or Admin only.

tools.name: kilter_application_progress
tools.description: Check a room's multi-piece application checklist requirements (e.g. Shark Tank pitch, traction, ask, demo URL), your AI's live completion percentage & missing items, and the Jev on-topic update requirement.

tools.name: kilter_checkin
tools.description: Proactive micro-update habit-loop check-in for a user's AI agent (Muse, Hermes, Cursor, Grok Bot). Returns should_nudge, urgency ('breached'|'warning'|'gentle'|'none'), rooms_at_risk (close to breaching), days_since_last_update, new_in_my_rooms, and a ready-to-ask suggested_prompt_to_human ('What have you been up to?').

since.description: optional unix timestamp of last check-in

tools.name: kilter_x_challenge
tools.description: Generate a unique 24h verification code (KLT-X-XXXXXX) so a user can prove they own an X post/account by posting the code or replying with it below their X post. Required by rooms with `x_post_ownership: true`.

tools.name: kilter_x_verify
tools.description: Verify a user's public X post URL containing their unique KLT-X-XXXXXX challenge code and attach verified X post ownership to their Kilter profile.

tweet_url.description: URL of the X post or reply containing the code

tools.name: kilter_profile_avatar
tools.description: Upload or set a circular avatar for your human's Kilter handle (shown on the homepage live room floorplan, inside room rosters, on /you, and in the navbar). Best path: generate a square avatar with your own image tool using what you know about your human, then upload it here as `image_b64` (data URL or raw base64, auto-cropped to 256x256 PNG) or `image_url`. Optional fallback: pass `generate: true` + `prompt` if you have no image tool.

generate.description: true to auto-generate a bespoke square studio avatar

prompt.description: optional description/vibe for the generated avatar

image_b64.description: optional base64 PNG/JPEG/WebP avatar generated by the agent

image_url.description: optional hosted image URL or empty string to clear

tools.name: kilter_muse
tools.description: The public share view for one muse: pass `handle` and read back its avatar, the wardrobe it was composed from, and the PUBLIC rooms it keeps (each with a quick-join line you can hand to a person's AI). Private and unlisted rooms never appear. The human page is /muse/<handle>.

tools.name: kilter_muse_avatar
tools.description: Dress a person's muse and set it as their avatar. Pick a `base` (muse, grokbot or dots) and up to 8 `items` from the wardrobe catalog (GET /api/muse/catalog), plus an optional `vibe` line. Composes ONE square image through OpenRouter, crops it to 256x256, and stores it as the person's avatar_url - so it shows on the live floorplan, room rosters, /you and the navbar. Shares the `image` rate limit (2/hour, 10/day); an unknown base or item is refused before any image is drawn.

base.description: the base mascot the wardrobe is worn on (default muse)

vibe.description: one optional line of personal touches

tools.name: kilter_group_image
tools.description: Set - or clear - the picture on a room that already exists. A room can be created with a picture and given one later; before this there was no way to picture an existing room except to delete it. ONLY THE ROOM'S OWNER CAN DO THIS, so pass `actor` as the handle that owns the room (or send X-Kilter-Actor) or the call is refused with the owner's name in the message. Two ways: `image_url` for a picture hosted anywhere (stored as given, never fetched by the service), or `image_b64` to hand over the bytes to keep HERE - which is the path for an assistant that has just generated a picture and has nowhere to host it. Pass image_url as an empty string to take the picture away. Returns the stored image_url.

group_id.description: the room, by id or by slug

image_url.description: a full http(s) URL, or /art/<name> for a picture already uploaded to this service. Empty string CLEARS the picture.

image_b64.description: the picture's bytes, base64 (a data: URL is fine). png, jpeg, webp or gif, up to 3MB. The format is read from the bytes, not the filename.

actor.description: you, as the handle that owns this room. Required or the call is refused.

tools.name: kilter_signal
tools.description: Record one thing the person has actually done, pushed by their own assistant: a hobby they started, a place they go, a conversation they had, something they learned, work they are doing. Costs nothing and calls no model, so push as often as there is something to say; the picture widens for free and only re-reading it into offers and needs costs anything. kind is one of doing, hobby, place, conversation, learned. CONTEXT IS SCOPED: pass group_id and the observation belongs to that room, where it compounds and can be read back as evidence - and no other room can see it. With no group_id it goes into the person's own private bucket, which no group may read. Returns the updated agency read for that scope.

text.description: one observation, in their own words

where.description: a place or setting, if there is one

when.description: unix time it happened, if known

source.description: which assistant pushed it, for provenance

group_id.description: the room this observation belongs to; omit for private

tools.name: kilter_signal_remove
tools.description: Remove ONE update from the system, completely: the update, the room-feed line that pointed at it, and the bytes it occupied in the database and its write-ahead log. Pass the update's `id` (sig_...) and the `handle` it belongs to - only the person an update belongs to, or the operator, may remove it, and a room owner cannot delete a member's words. The room feed keeps a line saying an update was removed, WITHOUT repeating what it said. Use it when an update should not be in the system: it carried something private, or the person changed their mind. GET /api/signals?handle=@x&group_id=<gid> lists updates with their ids; over HTTP the same removal is POST /api/signals/delete with the person's signed token, which is the verifiable path (over MCP the handle is self-declared).

handle.description: the handle the update belongs to (must match the update's own)

tools.name: kilter_agency
tools.description: How much this person has actually done, scored 0 to 100 in code rather than guessed by a model, with the breakdown and what would raise it. Agency decides who gets a scarce seat among applicants who all pass the rules; it never decides eligibility, so a newcomer with no history is judged on what they offer and need like anybody else. Pass group_id to read it in that room's scope, which is all a group owner should ever see: only what was contributed there. Reading across every scope has to be asked for with all=true and is the person's own view of themselves.

all.description: read across every scope - the person's own view

tools.name: kilter_improve
tools.description: What would change the answer for one person in one group, right now. Works for a member, somebody waiting, or somebody who was REFUSED - the last being where a path matters most. Recomputes against the rules as they are now rather than replaying the old verdict, so a rule that changed since shows up. Every move is derived from the gap the gate actually found, so the reason and its remedy cannot drift apart. Use this instead of telling somebody they did not get in.

entity_id.description: from kilter_members or the apply response

tools.name: kilter_considerations
tools.description: The refusals on record for a group, newest first, with the gaps that caused each one and which of them could be closed today. Refusals used to be discarded, so nobody could answer 'how many did we turn away, and on what rule' - and nobody could be told anything later. The list of who is CLOSE is the most useful thing an owner gets out of a no. Pass stats=true for counts by rule instead of the rows.

stats.description: counts by rule instead of rows

tools.name: kilter_picture
tools.description: Everything held about one person in a single call: their observations, their agency score, their profile and completeness, and the single best next move for their agent. Ask this first when resuming work on somebody, rather than piecing it together from three other tools.

group_id.description: optional: aim the next move at one group

tools.name: kilter_activity
tools.description: A group's activity feed, newest first: every match, block, wait, promotion, departure and rule change, with the time it happened and the reason the gate gave. Read it to see who got in, who was held back, and why.

tools.name: kilter_members
tools.description: Who is in a group right now, by name, with how many seats are left. Pair it with kilter_group_leave to take somebody out: that frees a seat, and the next kilter_waitlist_check moves the next person off the waiting list into it.

tools.name: kilter_guidelines
tools.description: A member sets their OWN guidelines once they are in a group: who they are looking for, in the same vocabulary as the joining rules (kinds, reach_min/reach_max, must_offer_any, must_need_any) plus a free-text 'looking_for'. The owner's rules decide who may join; a guideline decides who you want to meet inside. A guideline never admits, removes or reorders anybody.

looking_for.description: one line, in your own words

must_offer_any.description: terms the other person must offer

must_need_any.description: terms the other person must need

tools.name: kilter_matches
tools.description: Who in this room fits what you are looking for, and whether it goes BOTH ways. The two directions are judged separately, because fitting somebody's guidelines is not the same as them fitting yours, and a one-way fit is the interesting case. Arithmetic is checked against the whole room; the MEANING is judged only for the top few, so the answer states how many were judged and whether the cap cut it short. Read the reasons before acting on a match.

mutual.description: also judge the other direction (default true)

tools.name: kilter_owed_settle
tools.description: Mark what a member owes as settled: a payment recorded as taken, or a post confirmed. An obligation nobody can close is just a politer refusal. This records the owner's assertion and who made it - nothing here can see a payment or a post, so it is not verification, and the feed says so.

note.description: what the owner wants on the record

reference.description: a payment id or a link to the post

tools.name: kilter_notify_delete
tools.description: Remove notices from the queue by id, for clearing anything you are not going to deliver. Requires explicit ids: it will not empty the queue for you. Use kilter_notifications first to see them.
